name: OrcaRouter
notes: Router run by CONTINUUM AI PTE. LTD. (Singapore) that resells other companies' models behind one prepaid wallet and one sk-orca- key, with provider-prefixed model ids (openai/, anthropic/, google/ and so on). It is modelled as pay-as-you-go: OrcaRouter charges each upstream Provider's published per-token price with no markup and publishes no per-model price of its own, so each model's Cost is the original Provider's per-1M-token list price, taken from that Provider's Catalog file or its own pricing page; where the original Provider no longer lists the model, it falls back to models.dev's orcarouter entry, then to the original Provider's models.dev entry, as each model's notes say. The Hacker, Team and Enterprise plans are workspace governance tiers, not token allowances, so they are not modelled as Plans. Not Terms Risk: OrcaRouter publishes its inference URL for direct API use. Three chat endpoints, all with bearer auth: chat completions and Responses under /v1, and Anthropic Messages. OrcaRouter serves every chat model on chat completions and on Responses, translating for models whose upstream does not speak Responses; Claude models list Anthropic Messages first and GPT models list Responses first (ADR 0095), and the other models use chat completions only, since Responses reaches them only by translation and the docs offer Anthropic Messages for Claude models. No key was available for the live check on 2026-11-28: an unauthenticated request to each of the three endpoints answered HTTP 401 "Invalid API key" in OrcaRouter's error envelope, while an unknown path answered 404, so the routes are confirmed but no model was called, and the Provider ships Unverified. No exhaustedErrorCodes: 402 insufficient_user_quota (an empty wallet) stays a Cooldown, since topping up ends it at any time, as for the other prepaid resellers. 429 carries Retry-After; 403 has several causes (a key spend limit, a member budget, a key quota, a model outside the key's allow list), and 503 model_not_found means the model is not available to the account. Cached tokens are reported in usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and billed at the upstream's discounted rate; cache prices are the upstream's, and left empty where the upstream publishes none. The docs publish no complete model list (they point to GET /v1/models, which lists only what an account can use), so the shipped models are exactly the paid chat models the docs name. Named but not shipped, because neither the original Provider (its Catalog file or pricing page) nor models.dev (its orcarouter or original Provider entry) lists a per-1M-token price: openai/o1, openai/o1-pro, openai/o3-mini, openai/o4-mini, openai/gpt-4o-search-preview, google/gemini-3-pro-preview, grok/grok-4-fast-reasoning, grok/grok-4-1-fast-reasoning and grok/grok-3-mini. openai/gpt-5-search-api is not shipped either: OpenAI lists a per-1M-token price for it, but its searches are also billed per call (10 USD per 1,000 calls), which a per-token Cost cannot carry. Also not shipped: the -{effort} suffix aliases (such as anthropic/claude-opus-4.6-high and openai/o3-mini-high), which are a base model with a reasoning effort; anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5, which appears only in a metrics example; the orcarouter/ routers (auto, fusion, free), which pick a model per request at no fixed price; the -free models; Cyber models, which need the Security Research tier; and images, text-to-speech, video and the Gemini /v1beta protocol, which have no Protocol here.
